description: Physical surface parameters shared by every terrain source (see PLAN.md section 6 / P11): data/tracks/test_ground/terrain.json's per-cell surface ids and every feature mesh's per-triangle collision surface (test_ground_collision) both reference the ids in this file rather than embedding their own copy, so a later real-world land-cover source can map its classes onto the same ids/values.

fields.lambda_mu: Pacejka-style friction scale relative to dry asphalt = 1.0.

asphalt.source: Reference surface (lambda_mu=1.0 by definition). Crr for dry asphalt/concrete roads: Wong, Theory of Ground Vehicles, 5th ed., Table 1.3 (typical range 0.010-0.015; midpoint used).

kerb.source: Painted concrete: base Crr as asphalt (Wong Table 1.3); lambda_mu reduced ~10% from dry asphalt for the paint film, especially when wet -- illustrative test-ground estimate, not a measured value.

grass.source: Wong, Theory of Ground Vehicles, Table 1.3 / typical terrain friction-coefficient tables: firm turf mu ~ 0.35-0.45 dry, Crr ~ 0.06-0.10; midpoints used, flagged as a plausible published range rather than a specific measurement. [AS] lambda_mu 0.42 -> 0.6: owner 2026-10-12, uniform 0.6 pending a cited grass value (racing_game used 0.63 for game handling, RACE-002); crr unchanged.

dirt.source: Wong, Theory of Ground Vehicles, Table 1.3: dry, hard-packed dirt/gravel road, mu ~ 0.55-0.65, Crr ~ 0.03-0.05; midpoints used (plausible published range).

low_mu.source: Generic vehicle-dynamics references (e.g. SAE / SAE-adjacent tables cited by Milliken, Race Car Vehicle Dynamics, ch. 1) give unstudded-tyre-on-ice peak mu ~ 0.05-0.15; midpoint used. Crr assumed close to dry asphalt (smooth, hard surface) -- plausible range, not a specific measurement.

field.source: Wong, Theory of Ground Vehicles, Table 1.3: tilled/cultivated soil bracketed between firm dirt and loose soil, mu ~ 0.45-0.55, Crr ~ 0.08-0.10; midpoints used (plausible published range). Used by terrain.py's surface rules for the procedural farmland, not by any mesh here.
